title: Design System: The Pink Recipe Box

wordmark.purpose: "The Pink Recipe Box" top-left on the pink lid (header bar), in page cream.

display.purpose: The recipe title on its card, with the .ruled underline. 2.1rem on a phone, 2.6rem from 768px.

headline.purpose: Section names on and behind a card, and the divider tabs (1.2rem).

title.purpose: A recipe's name on its card on the wall; 1.3rem on a 1.65rem rule when written on the lines.

body.purpose: Ingredients, steps, descriptions; max 62ch. Cook mode steps rise to 1.6rem.

label.purpose: Button and chip text, tab-bar labels (0.9rem), Start cooking (1.15rem). Bold Source Serif; there is no sans.

hand.purpose: Margin notes, card counts, aisle names, captions. Regular weight on purpose: an aside, not a heading.

note.purpose: The single muted line under a card ("Mains · cooked 12×"); facts under a title at 0.95rem.

shadows.name: paper
shadows.purpose: An index card on the wall; the offset is the card beneath.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: A form sheet on top of a small stack.

shadows.name: card-sheet
shadows.purpose: The recipe read as one card on the counter; from 768px only.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: The generic Card container (settings, login, capture rows).

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Pink fills that float: Start cooking (#382a2226) and the camera tab.

shadows.name: leaf
shadows.purpose: A page in the flip-through view; pages still to come underneath.

motion.name: lid
motion.purpose: The tin's lid hinging open and the cards fanning inside it.

motion.name: tab-settle
motion.purpose: Divider tab dropping 1px to join the wall.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Index card active:scale(0.985); buttons use filter brightness(0.95) with no duration.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.effect: wall goes to 3 columns; Settings label appears

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.effect: column 45rem; recipe becomes a card sheet with two-column ingredients/steps; display 2.6rem

signatures.name: ribbon
signatures.css: position:absolute; top:-2px; right:14px; width:20px; height:34px; background:var(--color-pink); clip-path:polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,50% 78%,0 100%); box-shadow:0 1px 2px #382a2233

signatures.name: dog-ear-fold
signatures.css: position:absolute; right:0; bottom:0; width:26px; height:26px; background:linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 50%, color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-sink) 88%, var(--color-browned)) 50% 100%); border-bottom-right-radius:3px

signatures.name: splatter
signatures.css: five radial-gradient marks in browned, jam and butter; opacity: var(--splat)

signatures.name: tilt
signatures.css: rotate: ±0.6deg | ±1.2deg, hashed from the card id

signatures.name: ruled
signatures.when: a title or section heading on a card

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action that matters on a screen: Start cooking, Add, Put a card in. Box pink pill, cream text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.5rem; min-height:48px; min-width:48px; padding:0 1.5rem; border:0; border-radius:9999px; background:var(--color-pink, #c2566f); color:var(--color-page, #fdf6ea); font-family:var(--font-source-serif, 'Source Serif 4'), Georgia, serif; font-size:1.1rem; font-weight:700; box-shadow:0 2px 6px #382a2226; cursor:pointer; transition:filter 120ms, background-color 120ms; } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter:brightness(0.95); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-pink, #c2566f); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity:0.5; pointer-events:none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Everything else you can press on the back of a card: I made this, Correct this card, Cancel. Card paper with a pencil-line border.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.5rem; min-height:48px; min-width:48px; padding:0 1.5rem; border:1px solid var(--color-line, #382a2218); border-radius:9999px; background:var(--color-card, #fffcf6); color:var(--color-ink, #382a22); font-family:var(--font-source-serif, 'Source Serif 4'), Georgia, serif; font-size:1.1rem; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; transition:filter 120ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { filter:brightness(0.95); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-pink, #c2566f); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity:0.5; pointer-events:none; }

components.name: Search Line
components.description: One search line on the box page, filtering the wall in place. Card paper on the page (cream on a sheet), pink border on focus.
components.html: <label class="ds-search"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="20" height="20" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="11" cy="11" r="6.5"/><path d="m16 16 4.5 4.5"/></svg><input type="search" placeholder="Chicken, or a name you remember" aria-label="Search your recipes"></label>
components.css: .ds-search { position:relative; display:block; width:100%; max-width:32rem; color:var(--color-muted, #6f5a4b); } .ds-search svg { position:absolute; top:50%; left:1rem; transform:translateY(-50%); pointer-events:none; } .ds-search input { width:100%; min-height:48px; padding:0.625rem 1rem 0.625rem 3rem; border:1px solid var(--color-line, #382a2218); border-radius:0.75rem; background:var(--color-card, #fffcf6); color:var(--color-ink, #382a22); font-family:var(--font-source-serif, 'Source Serif 4'), Georgia, serif; font-size:1.05rem; caret-color:var(--color-pink-deep, #a8415a); } .ds-search input::placeholder { color:color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-muted, #6f5a4b) 80%, transparent); } .ds-search input:focus { border-color:var(--color-pink, #c2566f); outline:none; }

components.name: Divider Tabs
components.description: The tabbed dividers inside the box. The chosen one is cut from the wall's paper and joins it; the rest stand behind in sink. Wrapped rows fall back to chips.
components.html: 4 cards in the box

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Keeper / Want to try / Nope, Filed under, Cook this week. Unselected is card paper with a pencil line; selected fills pink ink. The dashed one names a new divider.
components.css: .ds-chips { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:0.5rem; } .ds-chip { display:inline-flex; height:48px; align-items:center; gap:0.375rem; padding:0 1rem; border:1px solid var(--color-line, #382a2218); border-radius:9999px; background:var(--color-card, #fffcf6); color:var(--color-ink, #382a22); font-family:var(--font-source-serif, 'Source Serif 4'), Georgia, serif; font-size:1rem; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 120ms, color 120ms, border-color 120ms; } .ds-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color:var(--color-pink-deep, #a8415a); background:var(--color-pink-deep, #a8415a); color:var(--color-page, #fdf6ea); } .ds-chip-new { border:1px dashed var(--color-pink-mid, #e8909f); background:transparent; color:var(--color-pink-deep, #a8415a); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-pink-deep, #a8415a); outline-offset:2px; }

components.description: One card on the wall: 3px corners, printed rules, a paper-edge shadow, a slight lean. Title in the hand on the lines when there is no photo; Keeper ribbon top-right, dog-ear and splatter once cooked.
components.html: Crispy Skillet Turkey BurgersMains · cooked 12×

narrative.overview:
Open the app and the recipes are already in front of you, as cards you recognise by sight. Everything in this system is a part of one physical object, a sun-faded pink recipe tin and the handwritten index cards inside it, and nothing is allowed to be a part of a website instead. The page is the counter the tin sits on, in flour cream. The cards are a whiter paper with faint printed rules. The pink is the tin itself, and it appears only where the tin would: the lid, a fabric bookmark, the one button that matters. A warm cocoa ink does all the writing.

Density is generous because this is used one-handed on a phone or at arm's length on an iPad, often with wet fingers and without reading glasses: 17px root type, a 48px floor on everything that can be tapped, two cards across on a phone. Imperfection is a feature, not a flourish. Cards sit at a slight lean that never resolves to zero; a cooked card picks up a folded corner and faint butter and jam marks that build with use and then level off. The rules of the paper are the one cool colour in the whole palette and they are only ever one pixel thick.

Two voices do all the type. Caveat, bold, is the hand that wrote every title, every divider, every heading and margin note. Source Serif is everything that is read: ingredients, steps, labels on buttons. There is no sans, no mono, no kicker, no badge row of metadata above a title.
keyCharacteristics: Paper, not panels: cream on cream, 3px corners, printed rules, tonal paper-edge shadows
One pink, used as the tin would show it: a lid, a bookmark, a primary action
Caveat for the hand, Source Serif for the read; no third face
Counter-scale ergonomics: 17px root, 48px tap floor, large pill buttons
Wear as a record: tilt, dog-ear, splatter, cook count, Keeper ribbon
The wall re-deals in place; narrowing never navigates away

rules.name: The Tin Rule
rules.body: Box Pink fills only what the tin itself would be: the lid across the top of the screen (the header bar), the primary action, the camera tab, the Keeper ribbon, the tins. It is never a page background or a card border.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Pink used as text or as a small selected fill is always pink-deep, never pink. The two are the same pink at two distances.

rules.name: The One Cool Note Rule
rules.body: The blue-grey rule is the only cool colour in the system and it appears only as a 1px line: card rules and the .ruled underline. Never as a fill, border, or text.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Every title, heading, divider, and margin note is Caveat. Headings are bold; asides are regular. No second handwriting face, ever.

rules.name: The Counter Rule
rules.body: Root type is 17px and nothing read mid-cook drops below 1.05rem. Inputs stay above the 16px iOS zoom threshold.

rules.name: The Re-deal Rule
rules.body: Choosing a divider or typing in search narrows the same wall in place and updates the address; it never navigates to a new screen.

rules.name: The Card Beneath Rule
rules.body: Offset shadows are always paper-toned (sink, or sink mixed with browned) and never ink-toned or black. They stand for the card under this one, not for height.

rules.name: The Phone Is The Card Rule
rules.body: On a phone a recipe has no frame or shadow; the page is the card. The sheet treatment appears only from 768px.

rules.name: The Paper Or Pill Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a card is 3px; anything that is pressed is a pill. Nothing is 8px-rounded-SaaS in between except an input (0.75rem) or a container Card (12px).

dos: Do write the wordmark on the pink lid in Caveat 700 at 1.75rem in page cream; the header bar is the one place pink spans the screen.
Do give every index card a 3px corner, the printed rule lines, the paper shadow, and a non-zero tilt from the set ±0.6° / ±1.2°.
Do set every title and heading in Caveat at weight 700, and every aside in .hand at regular weight in browned.
Do keep all tap targets at or above 48 × 48px and all read text at or above 1.05rem.
Do fill selected chips and small pink text with pink-deep, and reserve pink for the primary action, the camera tab, the ribbon and the tin.
Do make offset shadows paper-toned (sink) so they read as the card beneath.
Do narrow the wall in place when a divider or search changes, and keep the URL in step.
Do record wear with the three marks that exist (ribbon, dog-ear, splatter) and nothing else.
donts: Don't add a sans-serif, a mono, or a second handwriting face. Two faces, total.
Don't use pink as text on the paper; it falls short of contrast at small sizes. Use pink-deep.
Don't introduce any cool colour beyond the 1px rule line. No blue, purple, teal, or sage anywhere.
Don't use pure black, grey shadows, or 8px-rounded tiles for cards; paper is 3px and tools are pills.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a title, or a row of metadata badges; facts go in one muted line below the title.
Don't distress every card uniformly: splatter opacity is driven by cook count and caps at 0.5, and the dog-ear appears only once cooked.
Don't draw the joined divider-tab treatment when the row has wrapped; close the tabs into chips instead.
Don't render the Keeper ribbon or a card frame on a phone-width recipe; there the page is the card.
